Source is web/browser-only (rules 4/7): react-i18next useTranslation, lucide-react WifiOff SVG, the shared <AlertBanner> (not yet ported to native), and the @/hooks/useOnlineStatus hook (backed by navigator.onLine + window online/offline events via @/lib/resilience) have no native parity surface, and no @react-native-community/netinfo dependency is installed. A native-safe implementation was built per rule 7 with explicit documentation here and in the file header.

useOnlineStatus -> useNativeOnlineStatus: reads getConnectionStatus() from the parity web-parity/api/client.ts -- the same request-layer connection-status source of truth the web hook routes through lib/resilience (which the client also feeds). Because the native client exposes getConnectionStatus() but no onStatusChange broadcaster, the hook polls it every ONLINE_STATUS_POLL_MS (5000ms), clearing the interval on unmount so no timer leaks under --detectOpenHandles. status 'unknown' (cold start) and 'online' map to online=true (banner hidden); only 'offline' (a failed request) shows the banner -- preserving the web default of staying hidden on a connected device. State name `online` and the `if (online) return null` early-return are preserved verbatim.

useTranslation -> local useNativeTranslationFallback() returning the inline English fallback; the i18n keys pwa.offline.title and pwa.offline.banner and their exact English copy ("You're offline" / "Showing cached data. New requests will retry when you reconnect.") are referenced at the call sites so i18n intent is preserved (same pattern as BrowserCompatBanner / InlineCallout / EmptyStateThreshold).

AlertBanner variant=warning reproduced inline with View/AppText + shared tokens (no native AlertBanner exists yet, and importing it is impossible): flex items-start gap-3 rounded-xl border p-4 -> View flexDirection row, alignItems flex-start, gap spacing.md (12), borderRadius 12, borderWidth 1, padding 16; border-neon-amber/20 -> rgba(251,191,36,0.2); bg-neon-amber/5 -> rgba(251,191,36,0.05); title text-sm font-medium text-neon-amber -> AppText fontSize 14 weight semibold colors.warning (#fbbf24); body text-xs text-neon-amber/80 mt-0.5 -> AppText fontSize 12 rgba(251,191,36,0.8) marginTop 2. backdrop-blur-sm has no native analog and is omitted (documented).

WifiOff h-4 w-4 -> a decorative amber alert glyph in AppText (fontSize 16, colors.warning) flagged accessibilityElementsHidden + importantForAccessibility=no-hide-descendants to mirror the web aria-hidden icon. The boxed SemanticIcon `wifiOff` exists but renders a danger-toned bordered badge, heavier than AlertBanner's plain icon-in-title-color, so the inline glyph (matching the InlineCallout/BrowserCompatBanner glyph precedent in this directory) preserves the warning palette and inline weight.

Positioning: web `fixed bottom-[calc(4.5rem+env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px))] right-4 z-[9997] max-w-sm lg:bottom-[calc(1rem+...)]` -> an absolute anchor View (position absolute, right 16, bottom 72, maxWidth 384, zIndex 9997, pointerEvents box-none so the empty anchor never blocks touches). The lg:bottom-1rem desktop step has no native breakpoint so the mobile 4.5rem(72) base is used; env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px) collapses to its web-declared 0px fallback because no SafeAreaProvider is wired in this slice (documented in header).

No DOM elements, Recharts, Leaflet, framer-motion, or web UI components are imported; only react, react-native (View/StyleSheet), the shared AppText, the theme tokens, and the parity api client. role=status + aria-live=polite -> accessibilityLiveRegion=polite on the banner box (with `accessible` so the title+body are announced together); data-testid=offline-banner -> testID on the anchor. An optional testHookOnline prop is added as a native-only deterministic test seam; the propless `<OfflineBanner />` call site from the web source is unchanged.
Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit), npm run lint -- --quiet (eslint), npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles (jest).
